clue.text: Look round, touring bishop’s summerhouse (6)

indicators.note: to tour something is to go round it, so GAZE + O goes round B

blocks.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: A sightseer admires the bishop's garden summerhouse on a tour of the grounds.
annotation.walkthrough: GAZE and O sit side by side and then wrap round B, so the bishop ends up just before the final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open-sided garden building, which is what a summerhouse is.

clue.text: Postage reforms terrifying police officers (7)

indicators.note: the letters of POSTAGE are formed again into a new order

annotation.surface: A headline complaining that changes to postal charges are frightening the police.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reforms' reads as a plural noun about postal policy, but here it is a verb acting on 'Postage'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret police force of Nazi Germany, notorious for terror.

clue.text: Somewhere in Africa, extremists in Zambia rage (5)

indicators.note: the extremes of Zambia are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of ZAMBIA

annotation.surface: A news snippet about political extremists in an African country getting angry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' looks like political militants; here it means the letters at the two extremes of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997, a place in Africa.

clue.text: Alcoholic, in resting place, looked embarrassed (7)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, so the alcoholic lies within the resting place

blocks.note: a bed is where you rest
a lush is a heavy drinker

annotation.surface: A drunk wakes up in bed and goes red at what he remembers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alcoholic' reads as an adjective but is the noun: a lush is a drunkard.
annotation.definitionFit: To blush is to go red in the face from embarrassment.

clue.text: Friends perhaps arrive without energy after model (6)

indicators.note: COME is taken without its E (energy)
'after' means following in sequence, so the shortened arrival follows the model in the answer

blocks.note: to model for an artist is to sit
COME minus E, the physics symbol for energy

annotation.surface: Some friends turn up at a model's place looking worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Friends' looks like pals arriving; it is the American TV sitcom, and 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Friends was a long-running situation comedy, so it is an example of a sitcom.

clue.text: The setter’s appearance, eating starter from picnic hamper (6)

indicators.note: I'M AIR takes P inside, as if eating it
the first letter of picnic

blocks.note: the setter is = I'M, the setter speaking of themself
an air is a manner or appearance

annotation.surface: The setter describes looking the part while nibbling from a picnic hamper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' sits beside 'picnic' so it reads as a basket; it is the verb meaning hinder.
annotation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or hinder it, as to hamper it does.

clue.text: Insect Escoffier’s covering in batter, perhaps (9)

indicators.note: the covering of Escoffier is its outside letters, E and R

blocks.note: a cricket is a chirping insect

annotation.surface: The famous French chef coats an insect in batter.
annotation.walkthrough: Auguste Escoffier was a celebrated French chef, so 'batter' looks like cooking; here it is one who bats at cricket, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone who bats in cricket is one type of player of the game, alongside bowlers and fielders.

clue.text: Mother and child vacated rickety building (7)

indicators.note: rickety is emptied of its middle, leaving R and Y

annotation.surface: A mother and child move out of a tumbledown house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Building' reads as the rickety house they left; it is the definition, meaning stonework.
annotation.definitionFit: Masonry is stonework or brickwork, the stuff of building.

clue.text: Badenoch waits nervously to form opposition group (6,7)

indicators.note: a nervous state jumbles the letters

annotation.surface: Kemi Badenoch, Conservative leader in opposition, anxiously assembles her senior team.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: Kemi Badenoch leads the Conservatives in opposition, whose leading members form the shadow cabinet.
annotation.definitionFit: In British politics the shadow cabinet is the opposition's team of spokespeople mirroring government ministers.

clue.text: Sparkling wine, like vermouth, knocked back (4)

indicators.note: IT is sent backwards to TI

blocks.note: IT is Italian vermouth, as in a gin and it

annotation.surface: Two Italian drinks compared and downed in one.
annotation.walkthrough: IT for Italian vermouth comes from the old bar order 'gin and it'. 'Knocked back' suits drinking but works as a reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Playing up, thespian is most distressed (10)

indicators.note: the letters play about into a new order

annotation.surface: An actor who plays up on stage is thoroughly upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Playing up' looks like a phrase about misbehaving; 'Playing' is the indicator and 'up' belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the superlative: both forms mean sad or upset to the greatest degree.

clue.text: Gather nuts for Thomas’s predecessor (6)

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: Someone collects nuts to hand over to a man called Thomas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gather nuts' reads as foraging, with 'nuts' as the object; it is the indicator. Thomas is Thomas Tuchel, who succeeded Gareth Southgate as England football manager.
annotation.definitionFit: Gareth Southgate managed England before Thomas Tuchel took over.

clue.text: Commotion about queen and her partner carousing (8)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the commotion surrounds the queen
'and' means plus, so her partner is simply added at the end

blocks.note: a din is a noisy commotion
a queen's partner is a king

annotation.surface: A royal couple cause a stir by partying loudly.
annotation.walkthrough: D(R)IN + KING. 'Her partner' leans on the queen just mentioned.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to carouse is to take part in a noisy boozy party, so both words describe heavy social imbibing.

clue.text: Northern Irish region ignoring unknown Channel 4 programme (9)

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out of account, so the unknown is dropped from the region

blocks.note: County Down, one of Northern Ireland's six counties

annotation.surface: A TV channel overlooks Northern Ireland in its programming.
annotation.walkthrough: Countdown is a long-running British TV words-and-numbers quiz on Channel 4. Algebra's x, y and z are the crossword's unknowns.
annotation.definitionFit: Countdown is a Channel 4 game show, broadcast since the channel's first day in 1982.

clue.text: The latest update – Welsh fans going wild (9)

indicators.note: the letters run riot into a new order

annotation.surface: Breaking news: Welsh supporters are celebrating wildly.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a news report, so the definition blends into the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a brief item of the very latest news.

clue.text: Sojourn, for example, absorbing time (4)

indicators.note: 'absorbing' means soaking up and holding within, so the example takes time inside it

annotation.walkthrough: 'Sojourn, for example' tempts you to read the first two words together; 'for example' is SAY, holding T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean a spell spent somewhere as a visitor.

clue.text: Man on board privateer also with navy, primarily (4)

indicators.note: take the primary, first, letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Privateer Also With Navy

annotation.surface: A sailor aboard a pirate ship that has teamed up with the navy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' reads as a crew member on a ship; the board is a chessboard and the men are its pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are called men, and the pawn is the humblest of them.

clue.text: Rising cost of accommodation – blame associate (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters backwards

blocks.note: rent is what you pay for accommodation
to take the rap is to take the blame

annotation.surface: Rising rents are blamed on a business colleague.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising cost' reads naturally as inflation; 'Rising' reverses RENT RAP as the whole thing goes up the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a colleague you share a business or venture with.

clue.text: Two pubs with regularly filthy and inhumane behaviour (9)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals: fIlThY gives ITY

blocks.note: a bar is a pub, twice over

annotation.surface: A pub crawl through two grimy bars ends in savagery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the pieces; 'regularly filthy' sounds like a verdict on the pubs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes from 'barbarian', and names savage cruelty.

clue.text: Second-tier celebrity’s bit of damaged skin (7)

blocks.note: a celebrity one rank below the A-list, hyphenated in normal writing
a fluid-filled bubble raised by rubbing or burning

annotation.surface: A minor celebrity has a patch of damaged skin, as the gossip columns would report.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', linking the two definitions. The hyphen of B-LISTER vanishes in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A blister is a small raised bit of skin damaged by friction or burning.

clue.text: Widely proclaim president heartless egoist (7)

indicators.note: egoist loses everything between its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A political jibe calling a president a heartless egoist.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a political insult; 'heartless' is usually taken to remove just the middle letter, but here the whole interior goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the instrument's blast carries far, so to broadcast news loudly is to blow its horn.

clue.text: Where to see picture frames of Carracci, Nolde and Mantegna (6)

indicators.note: the frame of each word is its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of CARRACCI
first and last letters of NOLDE
first and last letters of MANTEGNA

annotation.surface: A gallery guide pointing out framed pictures by three painters.
annotation.walkthrough: Carracci, Nolde and Mantegna are painters, so 'picture frames' looks like an art gallery; the picture is a film and the frames are the outer letters of their names.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition resting on 'picture' in its old sense of a film, as in 'going to the pictures'.

clue.text: German tennis player, in good shape, initially ignores the writing on the wall (8)

indicators.note: the initial letter of ignores

annotation.surface: A fit German tennis star refuses to see the warning signs of her decline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The writing on the wall' is an idiom for a warning of doom, so 'ignores' seems to take it as object; here the phrase is meant literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Graffiti is literally writing scrawled on walls.

clue.text: Greek who flew from India, and American taking vehicle (6)

indicators.note: 'taking' means taking in, so the American holds the vehicle within

blocks.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A Greek flies in from India, and an American picks up a hire car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek who flew from India' reads as one air passenger; 'from' is only a link and India is the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wings of wax and feathers, too near the sun.

clue.text: The French invested in weapon, creating panic (5)

indicators.note: LA is clothed inside ARM, as one is invested with robes

annotation.surface: French money poured into armaments causes panic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invested' looks financial; its older sense is to clothe, so LA is wrapped in ARM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a sudden fright at danger.

clue.text: Hire soldiers before tense battle (10)

indicators.note: ENGAGE MEN is placed before T

blocks.note: to engage staff is to hire them

annotation.surface: A general recruits troops ahead of a nervy battle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the battle; it is the grammatical abbreviation T.
annotation.definitionFit: An engagement is a military battle between forces.

clue.text: Some current American representatives (4)

blocks.note: MPs, Members of Parliament, are representatives

annotation.surface: A remark about some present-day US congressmen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some current' reads as 'some present-day'; current is electric and amps measure it.
annotation.definitionFit: Amps are units of electric current, so a number of amps is some current.

clue.text: Are the stews warm again? (6)

indicators.note: to stew is to cook up, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: A cook asks whether yesterday's stews have been heated through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stews' reads as the noun being warmed; it is a verb acting on 'Are the'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym built the same way: RE- means again and heat means warm.

clue.text: Cue for performer in concert with piano – Beethoven’s Fourth (6)

indicators.note: the fourth letter of Beethoven

blocks.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

annotation.surface: A pianist waits for the signal to begin Beethoven's Fourth Piano Concerto.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Fourth' is surely a symphony or concerto; it is the fourth letter of his name. The Proms are a famous London summer concert season.
annotation.definitionFit: A prompt is a cue given to an actor or performer who has forgotten their line.
